D005-D006_h001.question:
Lately, things have been really tough, doc. It’s like my mind is playing tricks on me. For about two months now, I’ve been hearing voices. They aren't constant, but they pop up, sometimes whispering, sometimes a bit louder, and it's always unsettling, even when they're not saying anything specific. I also have this feeling, a strong one, that my boss, Sarah, is in love with me. I know it sounds strange, but I see the way she looks at me, the way she asks about my weekend – it all points to her having strong feelings. I know other people might not see it, but I’m convinced.

What's really getting to me is how I’ve been feeling on top of all that. I've had these incredible bursts of energy for ages now, practically since this whole thing started. I barely sleep, maybe two or three hours a night, yet I feel totally wired, full of ideas, and I talk so fast I can barely keep up with my own thoughts. I’ve been spending like crazy too, just buying things impulsively. This elevated mood has been present for most of the time I’ve been struggling with these voices and beliefs about Sarah. But here's the thing, there was this period, maybe a couple of weeks, where I was still hearing voices and convinced about Sarah, but I wasn't feeling all hyper and grandiose like I usually do. My mood was pretty flat then, but the other stuff was still there. It’s hard to manage my logistics job when my mind is racing and I'm convinced of these things.
D005-D006_h001.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h002.question:
It’s been a rough couple of months, maybe even longer. I've been feeling like people are out to get me. At work, I constantly feel like my colleagues are talking about me, watching my every move, and trying to sabotage my work, which is ridiculous. This even extends to my husband; I find myself questioning his intentions. I’ve also been seeing things – shadows moving in my peripheral vision, sometimes even people in the corner of my eye that vanish when I turn my head. It's been happening for about two months now.

Alongside all this, I've had huge bursts of energy. I barely sleep, maybe two or three hours a night, but I feel fantastic, like I could conquer the world. I’ve been talking super fast, buying a lot of things online, and generally just feeling incredibly restless and wired. This high-energy feeling has been going on for most of the time the paranoia and visions started.

But what really worries me is that for about three weeks there, the visions and the feeling that people were out to get me didn’t stop, even when I wasn’t feeling that wired, over-the-moon kind of energy. The paranoia and the shadows were just… always there. It’s not just mood-related.
D005-D006_h002.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h003.question:
It's been... rough. For the past couple of months, I've had this unshakable feeling that my former in-laws are somehow monitoring everything I do. I see movement out of the corner of my eye, even feel things crawling on my skin when there’s nothing there. It’s hard to focus at work when I feel constantly watched.

This whole thing started with me feeling incredibly energetic, almost unstoppable, about two months ago. I was sleeping only a few hours a night but felt fantastic, coming up with all these grand plans. That’s when the paranoia really kicked in, alongside those crawling sensations. But here’s the thing, even when I started to come back down to earth from all that energy, like after the first month or so, those unsettling feelings, the belief that I'm being watched and sensations on my skin, didn't go away. They've been persistent, even when I wasn't feeling those highs.
D005-D006_h003.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h004.question: Lately, things have been…intense. It’s been about two months now. This doctor, Dr. Miller, who comes into the ER sometimes – I *know* he’s in love with me. He sends me secret messages through the patient charts, little codes only I can understand. I hear his voice sometimes too, even when he’s not around, whispering how much he cares. At the same time, I’ve been feeling so unbelievably wired, like I could work three shifts back-to-back and not even break a sweat. My thoughts race, ideas just flood my head, and I barely sleep because there’s so much to do. This intense energy and these feelings about Dr. Miller, they seem to happen together, all the time. But for about three weeks there, right before all this energy kicked in, I was still hearing his voice and getting the messages, even though I felt pretty normal, not so high-strung.
D005-D006_h004.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h005.question:
Lately, things have been really intense, unlike anything I've experienced before. For the past couple of months, I've had this unshakable feeling that the new HR director, Ms. Jenkins, is completely infatuated with me. She keeps sending me these subtle signals, you know, a certain look or the way she pauses when I walk by. It’s hard to ignore. Simultaneously, I've been sleeping maybe two or three hours a night, feeling incredibly wired. My mind races with all sorts of brilliant ideas for improving factory efficiency, and I’ve been starting countless projects – though I sometimes struggle to finish them as new ideas pop up. My wife says I'm talking a mile a minute and easily agitated.

About three weeks ago, though, even as I was still feeling this incredible energy, things got stranger. I started feeling these odd crawling sensations on my skin, like tiny insects under my shirt, even when I knew there was nothing there. It was unsettling. The HR director still seems so interested, and my mind is still buzzing with all my plans, but those crawling feelings persisted, even later when my mood wasn't quite as high. It’s been happening for the better part of the last two months, this whole energized state. But it's those weird skin sensations, and the feeling about Ms. Jenkins, that have continued almost constantly, even during the few times I’ve felt a bit more “normal,” which has been for about three weeks now.
D005-D006_h005.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h006.question: "It's been a rough seven months, doctor. I just don't feel like myself. I used to love volunteering at the animal shelter, but lately, I can barely get myself out of bed. It’s like all the energy has been sucked right out of me. And then there are these thoughts... I know it sounds strange, but I truly believe that the news anchors are broadcasting secret messages just for me, especially when they touch their ear in a certain way. Sometimes, I find myself holding these odd positions for long periods without even realizing it until my joints ache. My daughter, bless her heart, says I 'light up' sometimes, that I’ll be talking a mile a minute, bouncing off the walls with ideas for new projects around the house that I never follow through on, staying up all night convinced I don't need sleep. She said I was like that for a good five months straight, full of grand plans and a strange sense of importance. The oddest thing, though, is that even when I feel perfectly normal and calm, those secret messages and strange feelings that people are talking about me still pop up, and they lasted for about three weeks when I was feeling quite level-headed, not all sped up or anything."
D005-D006_h006.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D006_h007.question:
"Lately, it feels like my body is just... wrong. I keep feeling this constant pressure, like my organs are twisting and contorting inside me. It started about seven months ago, around the same time I started having these shifts in my mood. I’ll go through periods of feeling incredibly revved up, hardly sleeping, and just buzzing with energy; I’ve been feeling this way for most of the seven months. Sometimes, when a patient moves a certain way, or a colleague makes a gesture, I find myself copying them without even realizing it – it's like my body just does it on its own. It's so embarrassing, especially at work.

Beyond that, I just can't bring myself to do anything. Getting through my shifts at the hospital feels impossible. I used to be so organized, but now even simple tasks feel monumental. There have been a couple of stretches, though, where I’ve still had these strange feelings about my body, these weird impulses to mimic others, and had absolutely no interest in anything, but the intense mood swings have settled down. Those periods have lasted for a couple of weeks at a time, where it’s just the weird thoughts and the difficulty getting going, not the racing highs."
D005-D006_h007.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D006_h008.question: Lately, things have been… different. My foreman keeps telling me I’m not focused, but that’s because I’m onto something huge out here. I’ve discovered a new way to extract oil, one that will revolutionize the industry and make me a billionaire. I’ve tried explaining it, but they just don’t get it yet. I’ve been feeling this surge of energy for about seven months now, barely needing sleep. My mind is racing with brilliant ideas, constantly moving, and I just can't sit still – I find myself pacing around the rig, often rubbing my hands together without even realizing it. The other guys have mentioned my face doesn't show much emotion sometimes, even when I'm talking excitedly about my discoveries. They just see a blank look. Even when I’m not feeling this intense energy, these thoughts about my invention, about my destiny, they're still there, strong as ever, and I’ve been dealing with them for the better part of a year.
D005-D006_h008.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D006_h009.question:
I’m not really sure why I’m here… My advisor told me I needed to come. She said I haven’t been myself for the past seven months, about the time I started thinking my stomach was rotting from the inside out. It's like I can feel it decaying, even though doctors say everything is fine. Sometimes I just refuse to do things, like going to class or even getting out of bed. It feels pointless. People say I’ve been flat, like I don’t react much anymore, but I don’t feel different.

I do remember feeling incredibly up for a few months – like I could conquer the world, barely sleeping, just churning out papers. My thoughts were racing, and I had so much energy. But even when that feeling faded, those strange beliefs about my body, and sometimes hearing voices, they just stuck around. For a couple of weeks, after the high had definitely come down, I was still so sure about my insides rotting, and hearing things, while everything else felt pretty low-key. It's only been a short while that I've felt pretty normal, but then these feelings of being "up" would start all over again.
D005-D006_h009.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D006_h010.question:
"It's been... I don't even know, maybe seven months now? Everything feels off. I keep seeing things, feeling things that aren't there. For instance, I'm absolutely convinced my kidneys are turning into stone, hardening inside me. I can feel the weight of it, even though every doctor I've seen says I'm fine. Sometimes, my face just contorts without me meaning to, like I'm pulling some weird, invisible string. People stare, and honestly, I just can't bring myself to react much. It's like my emotions are locked up, and my face feels stiff.

The thing is, alongside all this, I've had these intense bursts of energy, feeling like I'm on top of the world, full of grand ideas for plays no one else understands. Those periods, they've been pretty much constant for most of this whole ordeal, for longer than the times I've just been feeling... weird. But even when I'm not buzzing with energy, even when the 'up' feeling calms down, those strange thoughts and beliefs, like my petrified kidneys, they still stick around. They don't just disappear when the high goes away. It's confusing, like two separate battles happening at once, but the 'up' battle has definitely been the dominant one, playing out for the majority of these past months, though the other stuff has a way of lingering on its own."
D005-D006_h010.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D006_h011.question: I'm a 50-year-old HR Director, and honestly, things have gotten a bit out of hand. For about four months now, I've had these incredible surges of energy, where I genuinely feel like I'm a visionary, capable of solving global conflicts and revolutionizing corporate structures. I’ve even been speaking incredibly fast, sometimes repeating parts of what others say without realizing it. It's exhilarating but also exhausting, and these episodes have been pretty much constant for the whole four months. My husband says I'm not sleeping, and work performance has been a roller-coaster. The tough part is, even when I feel a bit more "normal" – not so high-flying or convinced I'm destined for greatness – these strange beliefs about my special powers still linger. For the last couple of weeks, even when I haven't been feeling this intense euphoria, those specific ideas about my abilities persist, quite strongly actually.
D005-D006_h011.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Delusional Disorder

D005-D006_h012.question: Well, Doctor, it’s been a rough few months, I tell ya. Ever since my Evelyn passed, I just haven't been myself. For about four months now, I’ve had this persistent feeling that the new neighbors, they’re watching me. Their curtains are always drawn, and I’ve caught them glancing over more than a few times. I find myself standing still for long stretches, just… frozen, sometimes in odd positions, like I’m waiting for something to happen. It's been going on for a long time, this feeling. But then, for the past month and a half, I've also been feeling absolutely fantastic, like I could finally repaint the entire house, something I haven’t had the energy for in years! I barely sleep, just a few hours here and there, and I’m full of ideas. It’s strange though, because even when I'm feeling this surge of energy and good spirits, sometimes those thoughts about the neighbors being after me are still there, clear as day, for weeks at a time, even when I'm not feeling so revved up. Actually, there was a good two weeks there, maybe even a bit longer, where I was just feeling paranoid and doing those odd postures, but without all the high energy.
D005-D006_h012.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Delusional Disorder

D005-D006_h013.question:
Lately, things have been really tough, Doctor. My husband, bless his heart, he’s been acting…different. I know he’s seeing someone else. I just *know* it. He denies it, but I’ve got my eye on him. I find myself watching everything he does, every text, every late night at work. It’s been going on for about four months now.

And it’s not just that. I’ve felt a wild energy, something I can’t turn off. I’ve been starting all these projects, rearranging furniture at 2 AM, talking a mile a minute. My thoughts race, and it's exhilarating, but also exhausting. This high has actually been around for most of the time I’ve been feeling this way, ever since the delusions really ramped up. There were even two weeks, not too long ago, where I was certain about his affair and doing all these strange things with my hands, almost like I was conducting some invisible orchestra, even though that intense, wired feeling had kind of died down. It’s like my mind just kept going with these beliefs, even when I wasn’t flying high.
D005-D006_h013.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Delusional Disorder

D005-D006_h014.question:
"It's like the world’s been ending every single day for the past four months. I keep thinking a great flood is coming, or the sky is going to fall, and there's nothing anyone can do. Even when I try to push the plates around at work, it’s like my arms get stuck in whatever position someone puts them in, heavy like lead.

But it's more than that. Most of the time, I'm buzzing with energy, barely sleeping, racing thoughts about how I can save everyone. I’ve been like that for ages, doing all night shifts, cleaning everything in sight, talking a mile a minute. The thoughts about the world ending and feeling like a statue started about four months ago, even though I've been ramped up for much longer. I just thought it was grief after my husband passed. But these last few weeks, maybe two or three, the sadness has lifted, and I'm still hearing whispers about the end of days, even though I don't feel like I need to save them anymore. It’s a relief to get a break from all that frantic energy, but the dread of the world ending is still very much there."
D005-D006_h014.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Delusional Disorder

D005-D006_h015.question:
I'm so exhausted. For the past four months, it feels like the world around me is just… crumbling. I see the news, and it’s like a confirmation: everything is falling apart. There’s this heavy feeling, this conviction that a massive catastrophe is coming, something truly destructive. It's not just a bad mood; it’s like a dark cloud over absolutely everything.

I’ve been so wound up, too. My mind races constantly, jumping from one idea to the next. I’ll start talking really fast, and sometimes I even find myself just repeating what someone else just said, just echoes of their words. It's been like this for much of the past four months.

What's really unnerving is that even when I feel a bit more balanced, not quite so over-the-top, those catastrophic thoughts, those dark predictions, they still linger. There was a stretch of a few weeks recently where I actually felt pretty normal mood-wise – not the heightened energy and not the intense dread – but those awful thoughts, the sense that everything was collapsing, they were still there, really clear in my mind.
D005-D006_h015.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Delusional Disorder

D005-D006_h016.question: It’s been a really tough few months, almost three now, since things started feeling off. Work, which I used to love, has become impossible. I’m a wedding photographer, but I can't even pick up my camera. I just feel so drained, and honestly, being around people feels like a chore. Lately, I've had these flashes of brilliance, thinking I have a direct line to the universe, that the song lyrics on the radio are hidden messages just for me, telling me to do extraordinary things. At the same time, I hear voices, sometimes whispering my name, sometimes full conversations in the background that no one else seems to hear. They often get quite jumbled, and I’ll try to explain what’s happening, but the words just come out like a garbled mess, making no sense at all. It’s been happening for weeks now, this surge of energy and these strange thoughts and sounds, all at once. Even when I’m not feeling so high, or not as agitated, those voices and the feeling that things are directed at me, they stick around. It’s like they linger after everything else calms down, for at least a couple of weeks, before the energy bursts back. It’s exhausting.
D005-D006_h016.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h017.question:
I'm 62, a security guard, and things have been… off. My wife, bless her heart, says I’m not myself. For the past three months, I’ve had this terrible feeling, like my insides are rotting. I keep smelling this awful, sweet decay, even when there's nothing there. It's gotten hard to explain things, too. My thoughts jump around, and sometimes what comes out… well, it’s just a jumble. People tell me I look blank, like I’m not really feeling anything, even when I am.

The strange thing is, for most of these past months, I’ve felt unbelievably energetic. Like I could work three shifts straight, no sleep needed. I was even trying to fix all the appliances in the house, talking everyone's ear off. But then, for about three weeks there, the energy just plummeted. My mood was normal, even a bit low at times, but those smells and the rotting feeling inside? They were still very much there, just as vivid as ever, even without the manic push. Then, the high energy came back, like a switch flipped. It makes me wonder what's going on.
D005-D006_h017.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h018.question:
"Lately, it's been a real struggle just getting through the day. For about three months now, my mind has been playing tricks on me. I've been tasting this strange metallic flavor, sometimes sweet, like burnt sugar, when there's nothing there. And these women – powerful, influential women – I just *know* they're sending me signals, telling me they're in love with me. It’s hard to explain, but it’s like I understand things others don’t, and I’ll use words like “sky-flighter” to describe a good day, but my wife just stares at me. The worst part is nothing feels good anymore. My daughter's laughter, the satisfaction of landing a plane safely...it's just flat.

It's been so intense; for the better part of these three months, I've also been feeling incredibly wired, like I could control every flight in the world simultaneously. I barely sleep, my thoughts race, and I get so irritable. But then, there was this period, maybe a few weeks ago, for a good two weeks, where I was still convinced about the women and tasting those weird flavors, but that buzzing, high-energy feeling wasn't there at all. I was just really flat and still experiencing those strange perceptions."
D005-D006_h018.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h019.question:
It’s… well, it’s been a lot. I feel like my brain's on fire. For the past three months, it's been getting worse. I see things, like shadows moving in the corner of my eye, or sometimes people standing there, just watching, and then they're gone. I know they’re not real, but it’s still unsettling. I also hear these voices sometimes, whispering about me, saying things like "glitch" or "debugged." It’s hard to explain, but it feels like there’s a whole conspiracy to undermine my work. I've even started making up words, like "code-drift" to describe how my thoughts jump around. It used to be that I loved testing games, finding all the little bugs, but now, nothing brings me joy. I could get a perfect score on a new game, and I just… don’t feel anything.

But it’s not just that. There have been times, for weeks on end, when I feel absolutely unstoppable. I pull all-nighters, convinced I'm on the verge of cracking the code of the universe, or coming up with the next big game concept. I’ve maxed out my credit cards buying new equipment for projects I barely start. It's like I’m flying, and the world is just too slow. These periods of intense energy have actually been going on for most of the past few months, pretty much ever since this whole thing started. Lately, though, even when I'm not feeling that burst of wild energy and hyper-focus, the shadows and whispers are still there, sticking around even when the intense moods lift.
D005-D006_h019.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h020.question:
Lately, it feels like my own mind is turning against me. Things started subtly about three months ago, but it’s gotten so much worse. I’ll be sitting at my computer, designing interfaces, and I’ll hear what sounds like whispers, almost like people talking about me just out of earshot. It's really unsettling. Sometimes, I hear voices calling my name, or commenting on what I'm doing. It’s hard to focus on work when that’s happening, and honestly, a lot of the time I just can’t bring myself to start anything creative at all.

Then there are these strong beliefs I have, like when I see a couple arguing down the street, I just *know* their fight is a coded message meant for me, or that certain news headlines are specifically written to give me instructions. My thoughts jump around so much; I’ll be talking about my new design project and then suddenly I’ll be on about how the coffee machine is spying on me. My husband gets confused because my sentences don't always track. This all really kicked off around the same time I started feeling this incredible surge of energy. For most of these past three months, I’ve been almost wired – sleeping only a few hours, buzzing with ideas, feeling on top of the world, making grand plans for my career and our shared future that even my husband thinks are a bit much. But there have been times, like the last couple of weeks, where those whispers and strange connections have continued even when that intense, wired feeling has completely faded and I'm just back to feeling flat.
D005-D006_h020.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h021.question:
Lately, it feels like my body is playing tricks on me. I've been convinced for about three months now that my liver is rotting from the inside, despite what all the doctors say. It’s hard to focus on work, pushing new drugs to clients, when I constantly smell something putrid, like rotting meat, that no one else can sense. I find myself making these strange hand gestures, almost like I'm conducting an invisible orchestra, especially during calls – it's unconscious. My husband notices, and it’s become really awkward.

This all started around the same time I began feeling incredibly wired and restless. For the past four months, I've had so much energy I barely sleep, just a couple of hours a night. I'll make grand plans for my sales territory, convinced I'm on the verge of a huge breakthrough, and talk non-stop to anyone who will listen. This heightened mood has definitely overshadowed the past few months. There was a stretch though, a couple of weeks, right after I first started smelling things and before my energy really peaked, where I still had the awful smell and the rotting feeling, but I wasn't feeling so sped up with these grand ideas the way I am now.
D005-D006_h021.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D006_h022.question:
Lately, it’s been a rough three months. I'm 31, a firefighter, and it feels like the world is teetering on the edge of destruction, like any moment a massive catastrophe is going to hit. I keep feeling these creepy-crawlies on my skin, like bugs are under there, even when I know nothing's there. It's distracting, especially at work. Sometimes, my wife will ask me to do something small, and I just... can't. It's not that I don't want to, it's like a wall goes up, and I just stare blankly.

The strange thing is, for most of these past three months, I’ve felt this incredible burst of energy. Like I could conquer anything, and sleep felt totally unnecessary. But then, for the last two weeks, that high energy vanished, and it’s just been the constant fear of disaster and those skin sensations, even without the manic feelings. It's really affecting my ability to do my job, and my wife is getting worried.
D005-D006_h022.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D006_h023.question: Lately, it’s like my body isn't my own. I've this deep-seated fear that my organs are… tangled up, or rotting inside, even though doctors say everything’s fine. And the tastes! For the past three months, everything I eat, or even just when I'm sitting around, has this metallic, sometimes bloody, flavor in my mouth. It's constant. My roommate even tried to move my arm the other day, and I just held it there for a while, like it was stuck. It's been a rough three months, to say the least, with these strange experiences and the racing thoughts and boundless energy. I’ve been feeling on top of the world for most of that time, like I could work for days without sleep, churning out video edits at lightning speed. But there was a stretch, about three weeks not too long ago, where I still had those weird tastes and the feeling about my insides, even though the intense euphoria and endless bursts of energy had calmed down. That’s probably the hardest part, when the weirdness is still there, but not the high with it.
D005-D006_h023.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D006_h024.question:
It's tough to talk about, Doc. Things have been... off. For about three months now, I've had these awful feelings that the forest, my whole life's work, is just withering away, dissolving into nothing. I keep hearing these whispers, too, always just at the edge of my hearing, usually telling me that it's already too late. Sometimes, my face just does its own thing, twisting into these funny shapes, and I don’t even realize it until someone points it out.

But it's not just that. For longer than these dark thoughts and whispers, since before they even started to feel constant, I've been on a real kick.
